source.title: IBNorm: Information-Bottleneck Inspired Normalization for Representation Learning
source.authors: Xiandong Zou; Jia Li; Xiao-Tong Yuan; Pan Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Compares normalization methods and reports held-out benchmark performance and information measures, but does not test the specific conditions or measurements named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study tests IBNorm against other normalization methods. It does not report training error alongside test error, so it does not measure the training–test gap described in the claim. The reported IB measures are not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study compares normalization methods using benchmark accuracy, estimated information-bottleneck values, and theoretical bounds. None of its comparisons tests V1–V8. Using AdamW, different model sizes, or fixed batch sizes does not test optimizer, width, or batch-size effects. Its information measures are not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim higher IB values and tighter theoretical generalization bounds, and report improved aggregate vision and language benchmark performance. Their discussion also acknowledges reasoning-task failures and limits evaluation to medium-scale language models. The empirical results do not directly establish smaller training–test gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Tests an information-bottleneck-inspired normalization intervention, rather than the claim versions' memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance depends on normalization variant and compression hyperparameter λ; the authors report moderate compression (λ = 4) performs best in the shown Llama 60M ablation and describe failure cases on reasoning-intensive benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: IBNorm-L improves reported top-1 accuracy over the stated baselines: ResNet18 95.57 versus 93.65, ResNet50 79.18 versus 76.15, and ViT 76.83 versus 71.54. ResNet recipes also differ in weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested IBNorm-L training recipes improve image-classification accuracy over the reported baseline recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Llama 60M has a higher reported Leaderboard II average with IBNorm-L; normalization-only training comparisons also report higher estimated token-level IB values with IBNorm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IBNorm can improve benchmark averages and estimated information-bottleneck values in the tested language-model settings.

record.code_released: not stated as a URL; authors say code will be released publicly and is available in the supplementary material.
record.problems: The results do not report training error alongside test error, so the train–test generalization gap cannot be checked. Several headline comparisons are reported as benchmark averages; uncertainty is given for selected Llama and GPT-2 results, but not for the vision table. The paper states that IBNorm has failure cases, including suboptimal results on reasoning-intensive benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Other benchmark averages and per-task results compare normalization variants but do not test any named claim version; the selected rows show the main reported image and language results plus the textual token-level IB comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the contrast between natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond the width needed for zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that change the batch-size penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and removal alongside weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, measured training–test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites original sources for general discussion of generalization, but does not test their version-specific findings. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not judgments that the reported normalization improvements are absent. Other normalization results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label accuracy.
Width sweep past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with IBNorm-L normalization and evaluated on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Authors state IBNorm-L exceeds BatchNorm by 1.92 percentage points.
rows.check: The reported 95.57 versus 93.65 accuracy comparison is correct but measures normalization performance, not any named version. Appendix F.2 also specifies different weight decay for IBNorm, so this is not an isolated normalization intervention.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with IBNorm-L normalization and evaluated on ImageNet.
rows.note: Table 3 reports the BatchNorm comparison for CNNs.
rows.check: The values were copied from the ViT columns. Table 3 reports ResNet50 top-1 accuracy of 79.18 for IBNorm-L versus 76.15 for BatchNorm. Appendix F.2 specifies weight decay 0.001 versus 0.0001, respectively. This method comparison bears on no named version.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.size_stated: 8 transformer layers, 8 attention heads, hidden dimension size 768, MLP dimension size 2304, and patch size 16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with IBNorm-L normalization and evaluated on ImageNet.
rows.note: Table 3 presents LayerNorm as the Transformer baseline.
rows.check: The 76.83 versus 71.54 values are correct for ViT, but this normalization comparison does not test convolutional versus fully connected networks or any other named version.

rows.subject: Llama 60M
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalization methods and evaluated on LLM Leaderboard II average score.
rows.uncertainty: not stated in Table 1; Appendix C.2 reports 0.1922 ± 0.0033 for LayerNorm and 0.2055 ± 0.0031 for IBNorm-L.
rows.note: Appendix C.2 reports three-run statistical results.
rows.check: Table 1 reports 0.2055 versus 0.1920; Table 8 separately reports three-run results of 0.2055 ± 0.0031 versus 0.1922 ± 0.0033. These are normalization-method performance results and bear on no named version.

rows.subject: Llama 130M
rows.operation_detail: Compared token-level IB values for normalization methods after training only the normalization layers.
rows.baseline: Variance-centric normalization; exact value not stated in text
rows.value: IBNorm consistently achieves higher values; exact value not stated in text
rows.note: The text gives the direction of the comparison; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The directional summary matches Section 4.3, but estimated token-level IB values cannot establish any named version, including V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship. Figure 2 evaluates these quantities on test data while only normalization parameters are trained.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
